logline: A kid who thinks red sheep are the prettiest thing in the world follows her blue lamb into the woods Dad is so boring about, hoping to find more red ones, and finds out why Dad dyes every sheep blue.
question: why tf is every sheep in the village blue?
premise: Every sheep in Ravenford is blue, all sixty: Dad won't let a white one through the gate ('He really likes blue') and counts them every night. 'They're our EYES, kid.' (Sheep can't even see that good.) Last spring one came back from the woods red, the prettiest one ever; Dad sat at the gate with his crossbow for a week (she thinks he wanted more red ones); one night the trees went snap, snap, snap, like clapping. Today she forgets to shut the gate, her lamb gets out, Dad is boring about the woods, so she goes in happily to find more red ones.
twist: The sheep are an alarm. In vanilla Java an evoker that isn't fighting casts its 'wololo' spell on a BLUE sheep within 16 blocks and turns it RED (minecraft.wiki/w/Evoker 'Sheep color conversion spell'; Evoker.EvokerWololoSpellGoal; mobGriefing on; only blue ones, which is why Dad dyes every white one). One lives in the woods. She went in to find more red ones. In the trees the lamb stops; a faint 'wololo'; beyond the lamb an evoker with its arms raised, and the lamb's wool turns red. The arms drop and its head turns to her. Cut. 'They're our EYES' was literal: blue means safe, red means an evoker is near. The snaps a year ago were its fangs.
